questions.question:
Three statements are given, followed by Three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

No number is a machine.

Not a single machine is a bowl.

Every bowl is a sink.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some sinks which are bowls are numbers as well.

II. No number is a bowl.

III. Some sinks are bowls.

options.text: Only conclusions II and III follow
All conclusions, I, II and III, follow
Either conclusion I or II follows

questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as shown below :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c45d1b6f7af35e8e7bfccc45cdbc15f005075aa663c21c47bdd854445875b3f6.png] 

Conclusions:

I. Some sinks which are bowls are numbers as well → Does not follow (As every bowl is a sink, not a single machine is a bowl and no number is a machine. As no bowl cannot be machine which cannot be bowl which whole comes in sink, therefore, some sinks which are bowls cannot be numbers, thus is false.)

II. No number is a bowl → Does not follow (As every bowl is a sink, not a single machine is a bowl and no number is a machine. As no direct relation is given between bowl and number therefore it is false.)

III. Some sinks are bowls → **Follow **(As every bowl is a sink. As whole bowl comes in sink, therefore some sinks are bowl is true.)

∴ Here, Only conclusion III follows.​

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 4"

questions.question: In 1908 Khudiram Bose along with _________ was involved in throwing a bomb at a carriage believing it to be occupied by Kingsford, the then sitting judge of Muzaffarpur.

• Khudiram Bose and Prafulla Chaki were both young revolutionaries who were part of the Indian independence movement against British rule.
 
• Their act was aimed at retaliating against the repressive actions of the British authorities.
 
• Unfortunately, the bomb missed its target and instead killed two British women, resulting in severe consequences for both revolutionaries.

• **Prafulla Chaki** managed to evade capture initially but eventually took his own life to avoid arrest.
 
• Their sacrifice became a significant moment in the history of India's struggle for independence and inspired many young Indians to join the revolutionary movement.
 
• Their story is a poignant reminder of the courage and determination displayed by the freedom fighters of India.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT considered a method of conservation of natural resources?

__
 
• **Extraction** is not considered a method of conservation of natural resources.
 
• Conservation methods typically include practices that help preserve and protect natural resources, such as **afforestation, recycling, and terrace farming**.
 
• **Afforestation** refers to planting trees to create forests, which helps in maintaining ecological balance.
 
• **Recycling** involves converting waste materials into reusable materials, thereby reducing the need for new raw materials.
 
• **Terrace farming** is an agricultural practice that prevents soil erosion and conserves water.

• **Natural resource conservation** is essential for sustainable development and ensuring that resources are available for future generations.
 
• Methods such as **afforestation** and **recycling** help in reducing the environmental impact and preserving biodiversity.
 
• **Extraction**, on the other hand, often depletes natural resources and can cause significant environmental damage if not managed sustainably.
 
• Conservation efforts focus on sustainable practices to maintain the health of ecosystems and the availability of resources.

questions.question: Using Fleming’s right-hand rule, in which direction will the current flow if the direction of magnetic field is towards north and the conductor is moving vertically upward?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Towards west**__

__
 
• Using **Fleming's right-hand rule**, if the direction of the magnetic field is towards north and the conductor is moving vertically upward, the current will flow towards the west.
 
• Fleming's right-hand rule states that if you extend the thumb, forefinger, and middle finger of your right hand such that they are mutually perpendicular, with the thumb pointing in the direction of motion of the conductor, and the forefinger in the direction of the magnetic field, then the middle finger will point in the direction of the induced current.
 
• In this scenario, with the magnetic field towards the north and the conductor moving upward, the thumb points upward, the forefinger points north, and the middle finger points towards the west.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fleming's right-hand rule** is used to determine the direction of induced current in a conductor moving in a magnetic field.
 
• It is particularly useful in the context of generators and other devices where mechanical motion is converted into electrical energy.
 
• Conversely, **Fleming's left-hand rule** is used for electric motors where electrical energy is converted into mechanical motion.
 
• Both rules are fundamental principles in electromagnetism and are widely used in physics and engineering.

questions.question: A dealer sells an article at ₹850 after offering a cash discount of 15% on its marked price. Without discount, he would have earned a profit of 25%. What is the cost price of the article (in ₹)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Selling Price (SP) = ₹850, Discount = 15% ⇒ MP = 850 × (100 ÷ 85) = ₹1000

Without discount, SP = MP = ₹1000.

Profit = 25% ⇒ CP = 1000 × (100 ÷ 125) = ₹800.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹800.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Selling price with discount (SP) = ₹850

Discount percentage = 15%

Profit percentage without discount = 25%

**Formula Used:**

MP = SP × [100 ÷ (100 − Discount%)]

CP = SPₙₑw × [100 ÷ (100 + Profit%)]

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b4badddf2e39a2023bbcaf1591366c7ac1565341460173f8e0a6f36a5b851b0d.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let Marked Price be MP.

⇒ SP = MP − 15% of MP = 0.85 × MP

⇒ 850 = 0.85 × MP

⇒ MP = 850 × (100 ÷ 85) = ₹1000

⇒ Without any discount, the dealer sells the article at its Marked Price.

⇒ So, New Selling Price (SPₙₑw) = MP = ₹1000

⇒ At this price, Profit = 25%

⇒ CP + 25% of CP = SPₙₑw

⇒ 1.25 × CP = 1000

⇒ CP = 1000 × (100 ÷ 125)

⇒ CP = ₹800

**∴ The correct answer is ₹800.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP). The formula directly yields: Selling Price = MP × (1 − Discount%).

Profit/Loss Without Discount

When a shopkeeper gives no discount on an item, the Selling Price becomes equal to the Marked Price (SP = MP). Under this condition, Profit or Loss percentage is directly estimated over the Cost Price leading up to the MP.

Effective Multipliers Rule

For a given profit of P%, the selling price multiplier translates to SP = CP × (1 + P/100). Similarly, for a discount of D%, SP = MP × (1 − D/100). Equating both sides helps find any missing variable quickly.

questions.solution:
**Given:**

A can complete the work in 9 days.

B can complete the work in 12 days.

C can complete the work in 18 days.

Work done by a person in 1 day = 1 / Number of days to complete work

Remaining work = 1 - (7 / 12)

Work done by C in 1 day = 1 / 18

Remaining work = Work done by C in x days

(5)/(12) = (x)/(18)

⇒ x = (5 / 12) × 18

⇒ x = (5 × 18) / 12

⇒ x = 90 / 12

**The number of days C took to complete the work is 7.5 days.**
